style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;fontSize=10;" value="<b style="color:#1565c0">── DIRECT PROJECTION PATH ──</b>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="18" width="280" x="130" y="190" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_td" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#bbdefb;strokeColor=#1565c0;fontSize=10;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>TimeDistributed Dense(64, activation=None)</b><br>Applies same Dense(64) at each of T timesteps<br>Linear projection (no activation)<hr><b>Input:</b> (B, T, F_in) → <b>Output:</b> (B, T, 64)<br><b>Name:</b> td_proj" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="340" x="120" y="215" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="td_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY:</b> Projects input to same dimensionality (64)<br>as the LSTM output. This creates a "shortcut"<br>that the residual gate can use to bypass the LSTM<br>when the LSTM output is not informative.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="55" width="310" x="80" y="305" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="right_title" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;fontSize=10;" value="<b style="color:#7b1fa2">── TEMPORAL MODELING PATH ──</b>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="18" width="280" x="680" y="190" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_bilstm" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1bee7;strokeColor=#7b1fa2;fontSize=10;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>Bidirectional LSTM(units=64)</b><br>return_sequences=True<br>Forward LSTM(64) + Backward LSTM(64)<hr><b>Input:</b> (B, T, F_in)<br><b>Output:</b> (B, T, 128) = 64 fwd + 64 bwd concatenated" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="380" x="650" y="215" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bilstm_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY BiLSTM:</b> Forward LSTM captures past→present<br>dependencies; backward captures present→past.<br>For activity recognition, future frames provide context<br>(e.g., arm raise followed by wave = waving, not stretching).<br>return_sequences=True keeps temporal dimension.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="340" x="850" y="305" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_lproj" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1bee7;strokeColor=#7b1fa2;fontSize=10;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>TimeDistributed Dense(64)</b><br>Project BiLSTM output from 128 → 64<hr><b>Input:</b> (B, T, 128) → <b>Output:</b> (B, T, 64)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="320" x="680" y="400" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_drop1" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#9e9e9e;fontSize=10;" value="<b>Dropout(rate=0.2)</b><br><b>In/Out:</b> (B, T, 64)<br><b>Name:</b> lstm_proj" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="240" x="720" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="drop_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY:</b> Dropout randomly zeros 20% of LSTM<br>output neurons during training. Prevents<br>co-adaptation and reduces overfitting.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="45" width="220" x="970" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_cat" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e0e0e0;strokeColor=#616161;fontSize=10;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>⊕ Concatenate(axis=−1)</b><br>[td_proj, lstm_proj] along feature axis<hr><b>Input:</b> (B,T,64) + (B,T,64) → <b>Output:</b> (B, T, 128)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="55" width="530" x="310" y="580" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="cat_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY:</b> The gate must see BOTH the direct projection<br>AND the LSTM output to learn which to favor.<br>Concatenation gives the gate full context.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="45" width="280" x="860" y="580" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_gate" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff9c4;strokeColor=#f9a825;fontSize=10;strokeWidth=2;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>σ Sigmoid Gate</b><br>TimeDistributed Dense(64, activation="sigmoid")<br>Outputs values ∈ [0, 1] per feature per timestep<hr><b>Input:</b> (B, T, 128) → <b>Output:</b> (B, T, 64)<br><b>Name:</b> gate" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="530" x="310" y="680" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="gate_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY SIGMOID GATE:</b><br>• gate=1.0 → fully trust LSTM temporal features<br>• gate=0.0 → fully trust direct projection (identity-like)<br>• gate=0.5 → equal blend<br>This is learned per-feature per-timestep, allowing<br>the model to dynamically decide what information<br>to route through the LSTM vs. bypass it.<br>Similar concept to GRU's update gate.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="280" x="860" y="680" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="split2_lbl" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;fontSize=10;fontColor=#333;" value="<b><font style="color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">↓ Gate splits into two complementary paths ↓</font></b>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="18" width="450" x="350" y="792" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_gmul" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#c8e6c9;strokeColor=#2e7d32;fontSize=10;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>⊗ Multiply</b><br>gate × lstm_proj<br>(element-wise)<hr><b>Input:</b> 2 × (B,T,64) → <b>Output:</b> (B,T,64)<br><b>Name:</b> gated (LSTM signal weighted by gate)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="340" x="140" y="820" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_inv" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff9c4;strokeColor=#f9a825;fontSize=10;" value="<b>Lambda: 1.0 − gate</b><br>Compute inverse gate<hr><b>In/Out:</b> (B, T, 64)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="280" x="680" y="810" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_rmul" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#c8e6c9;strokeColor=#2e7d32;fontSize=10;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b>⊗ Multiply</b><br>(1 − gate) × td_proj<br>(element-wise)<hr><b>Input:</b> 2 × (B,T,64) → <b>Output:</b> (B,T,64)<br><b>Name:</b> residual (direct signal weighted by 1−gate)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="340" x="660" y="880" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="res_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY COMPLEMENTARY GATING:</b><br>gate + (1−gate) = 1.0 always.<br>This ensures the total signal magnitude<br>is preserved. The model learns a soft<br>routing between LSTM path and direct path.<br>When gate→0, gradients flow through td_proj<br>(residual path) preventing vanishing gradients.</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="280" x="140" y="920" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_add" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#bbdefb;strokeColor=#1565c0;fontSize=10;strokeWidth=2;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b style="font-size:12px">⊕ Add</b><br>gated + residual = gate·lstm + (1−gate)·proj<hr><b>Input:</b> 2 × (B,T,64) → <b>Output:</b> (B, T, 64)<br><b>Name:</b> out (gated residual output)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="65" width="530" x="310" y="1040" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="add_formula" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font style="font-size:11px;color:#0d47a1"><b>Mathematical Formula:</b><br>out = σ(W_g · [td_proj ⊕ lstm_proj]) · lstm_proj<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;+ (1 − σ(W_g · [td_proj ⊕ lstm_proj])) · td_proj</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="530" x="310" y="1115" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_skip_add" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffcdd2;strokeColor=#c62828;fontSize=10;strokeWidth=3;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;" value="<b style="font-size:12px">⊕ Skip Connection Add (Block 2 Only)</b><br>out + block1_output<hr><b>Input:</b> 2 × (B,T,64) → <b>Output:</b> (B, T, 64)<br><b>Name:</b> final_out" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="65" width="530" x="310" y="1200" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="skip_why" parent="1" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;" value="<font color="#b71c1c" style="font-size:9px"><b>WHY INTER-BLOCK SKIP:</b><br>Block 1 captures initial temporal features.<br>Block 2 refines them. The skip connection ensures<br>Block 1's features are not lost through Block 2's<br>processing. Also provides a direct gradient path<br>from loss back to Block 1 (ResNet principle).</font>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="280" x="860" y="1200" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bk_out" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#f57f17;fontSize=11;strokeWidth=3;" value="<b style="font-size:13px">BLOCK OUTPUT</b><br><b>Shape: (B, T, 64)</b><br>→ to next block (Block 2) or GlobalAveragePooling1D" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="55" width="410" x="370" y="1310" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ext_skip_in" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffcdd2;strokeColor=#c62828;fontSize=9;strokeWidth=2;dashed=1;" value="<b>Block 1 output</b><br>(external skip)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="130" x="140" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ext_skip_arrow" edge="1" parent="1" source="ext_skip_in" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;strokeColor=#c62828;strokeWidth=2;dashed=1;" target="bk_skip_add"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ea_1" edge="1" parent="1" source="bk_in" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;strokeColor=#555;" target="bk_td"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ea_2" edge="1" parent="1" source="bk_in" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;strokeColor=#555;" target="bk_bilstm"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ea_3" edge="1" parent="1" source="bk_bilstm" WHY: Dropout randomly zeros 20% of LSTM
output neurons during training. Prevents
co-adaptation and reduces overfitting.

⊕ Concatenate(axis=−1)
[td_proj, lstm_proj] along feature axisInput: (B,T,64) + (B,T,64) → Output: (B, T, 128)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 577px; margin-left: 863px;

div.font:
WHY: The gate must see BOTH the direct projection
AND the LSTM output to learn which to favor.
Concatenation gives the gate full context.

switch.text: WHY: The gate must see BOTH the direct project...

div.div:
σ Sigmoid Gate
TimeDistributed Dense(64, activation="sigmoid")
Outputs values ∈ [0, 1] per feature per timestepInput: (B, T, 128) → Output: (B, T, 64)
Name: gate

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 677px; margin-left: 863px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;
div.font:
WHY SIGMOID GATE:
• gate=1.0 → fully trust LSTM temporal features
• gate=0.0 → fully trust direct projection (identity-like)
• gate=0.5 → equal blend
This is learned per-feature per-timestep, allowing
the model to dynamically decide what information
to route through the LSTM vs. bypass it.
Similar concept to GRU's update gate.

b.font: ↓ Gate splits into two complementary paths ↓

div.div:
⊗ Multiply
gate × lstm_proj
(element-wise)Input: 2 × (B,T,64) → Output: (B,T,64)
Name: gated (LSTM signal weighted by gate)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 278px; height: 1px; padding-top: 825px; margin-left: 682px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;

div.div:
Lambda: 1.0 − gate
Compute inverse gateIn/Out: (B, T, 64)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 322px; height: 1px; padding-top: 910px; margin-left: 670px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
⊗ Multiply
(1 − gate) × td_proj
(element-wise)Input: 2 × (B,T,64) → Output: (B,T,64)
Name: residual (direct signal weighted by 1−gate)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 917px; margin-left: 143px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;
div.font:
WHY COMPLEMENTARY GATING:
gate + (1−gate) = 1.0 always.
This ensures the total signal magnitude
is preserved. The model learns a soft
routing between LSTM path and direct path.
When gate→0, gradients flow through td_proj
(residual path) preventing vanishing gradients.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 512px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1063px; margin-left: 320px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
⊕ Add
gated + residual = gate·lstm + (1−gate)·projInput: 2 × (B,T,64) → Output: (B, T, 64)
Name: out (gated residual output)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1112px; margin-left: 313px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;
div.font:
Mathematical Formula:
out = σ(W_g · [td_proj ⊕ lstm_proj]) · lstm_proj
+ (1 − σ(W_g · [td_proj ⊕ lstm_proj])) · td_proj

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 512px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1223px; margin-left: 320px;

div.div:
⊕ Skip Connection Add (Block 2 Only)
out + block1_outputInput: 2 × (B,T,64) → Output: (B, T, 64)
Name: final_out

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1197px; margin-left: 863px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;
div.font:
WHY INTER-BLOCK SKIP:
Block 1 captures initial temporal features.
Block 2 refines them. The skip connection ensures
Block 1's features are not lost through Block 2's
processing. Also provides a direct gradient path
from loss back to Block 1 (ResNet principle).
